title: D-Wave Quantum Just Announced an Expanded Deal. Should You Buy the Stock Now?
author: Catie Hogan
description: D-Wave Quantum announced an expanded deal with AT&T to use its quantum computing technology across network operations. The pilot program demonstrated a 240x improvement in processing time for network optimization. While the stock is down 26% in 2026, the AT&T partnership and 563% year-over-year increase in remaining performance obligations signal potential traction, though the company remains highly speculative with significant losses relative to revenue.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Expanded AT&T deal demonstrates real-world commercial applicability with impressive 240x performance improvement. Strong increase in remaining performance obligations (563% YoY) signals growing business traction and potential market validation for quantum computing technology.

AT&T's expansion of D-Wave technology use is positive for D-Wave but represents a minor operational development for AT&T. The partnership demonstrates confidence in quantum solutions but has limited material impact on AT&T's overall business.

title: Why D-Wave Quantum Stock Surged Today
author: Joe Tenebruso
description: D-Wave Quantum's stock surged 20.20% after expanding its partnership with AT&T. Early tests showed D-Wave's quantum technology reduced AT&T's network optimization process runtime from one hour to under 15 seconds. AT&T plans to expand the technology to outage detection, network planning, and traffic management. Benchmark analyst Gary Mobley maintains a buy rating with a $30 price target, representing over 50% upside.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock surged 20.20% on expanded AT&T partnership demonstrating practical quantum advantage with significant performance improvements (60x speedup). Analyst maintains buy rating with 50%+ upside target, and company is delivering real-world solutions unlike competitors.

Expanding quantum computing partnership with D-Wave to optimize network operations, reduce processing time dramatically, and modernize infrastructure. Demonstrates adoption of cutting-edge technology to improve efficiency and real-time operations.

title: AT&T Stock Has Been Quietly Rallying Since the Start of July. After a Strong Q2, Is It Due to Soar Even Higher?
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: AT&T stock has rallied 18% since early July as SpaceX struggles, recovering from earlier concerns about competitive disruption. The company posted solid Q2 earnings with $31.6B in revenue and strong customer additions (646K internet net adds, 432K postpaid phone net adds). Trading at 10x forward earnings with a 4.6% dividend yield, analysts suggest the stock has further upside potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 earnings with revenue growth and robust customer additions in both internet and wireless segments. Stock rallying 18% since July with attractive valuation at 10x forward earnings and high 4.6% dividend yield. Market concerns about SpaceX competition appear overblown.

title: Why Quantum Computing Stock Just Popped
author: Rich Smith
description: Quantum Computing (QUBT) stock gained 5.8% after competitor D-Wave Quantum announced AT&T signed a contract to use D-Wave's annealing quantum computing technology for network optimization. Despite not being party to the deal, QUBT rose on speculation that AT&T's broader quantum computing strategy could benefit multiple vendors. However, analysts note Quantum Computing has fewer major contracts than D-Wave and must deliver on forecasted $41 million revenue (10x growth) to justify investor optimism.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock gained 5.8% on positive sentiment from AT&T's quantum computing strategy announcement, though the company wasn't directly involved in the deal. Analysts forecast 10x revenue growth, but execution risk remains high given limited major contracts to date.
Stock surged 16.19% following announcement of AT&T contract to use D-Wave's annealing quantum computing technology for network operations and optimization, representing a significant commercial win.

Stock gained 1.24%, a modest increase. While the quantum computing partnership is strategically important, it represents one component of AT&T's broader innovation strategy and had limited market impact.

title: Why Rigetti Computing Stock Just Popped
author: Rich Smith
description: Rigetti Computing stock jumped 7.7% after competitor D-Wave Quantum announced a partnership with AT&T to use its quantum computing technology. Additionally, Benchmark analyst David Williams initiated coverage of Rigetti with a buy rating and $25 price target, suggesting 67% upside potential. However, analysts caution that quantum computing profits remain years away and recommend a portfolio approach to the sector.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock gained 7.7% on positive sector momentum from competitor's AT&T deal, plus new buy rating from Benchmark analyst with $25 price target implying 67% upside. However, sentiment is tempered by acknowledgment that profitability remains 5+ years away.
